elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Section 16.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetrical in party direction, and no retained language leaves either Party uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 16.7 caps at "the fees and other amounts payable by Ono ... during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" with no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor and no "paid or payable" formulation; the base is also "fees and other amounts payable", which is not the same noun set as "fees paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY" — mutual, and untouched by the redline.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 excepts "either Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10 (Confidentiality)" from the cap; the caption at p0520 confirms Article X is Confidentiality.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears in the operative text.
16.7 excepts "each Party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement (including under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2)" — mirrors the indemnity sources 16.5 itself identifies.
16.7: "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct" sits outside the cap; consistent with the existing 16.5 proviso.
16.7 expressly excepts "willful misconduct" for either Party.
No fraud carve-out appears in 16.7 or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 contains no IP-infringement carve-out; the indemnification carve-out does not expressly cover direct claims for infringement of the other Party's IP.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing states that Ono's payment obligations (milestones, royalties, other amounts payable) are not "damages" for cap purposes; as drafted the new cap could be read to limit Ono's own payment liability, which Array will resist.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 16.7 applies to "each Party's total aggregate liability"; no one-sided or unlimited-Customer language remains.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 16.7 measures the cap by "the fees and other amounts payable by Ono under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee-based basis; "fees" are expressly within the base.
Carve-out for "each Party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement (including under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2)"; indemnities therefore sit outside the cap (no super-cap issue).

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out for "either Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10 (Confidentiality)".
Carve-out for "willful misconduct" in the same exception clause.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the inserted Section 16.7 delivers a mutual aggregate cap measured by 12 months of amounts payable by Ono, with indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation, because the Agreement previously contained only the Section 16.5 consequential-damages waiver and no aggregate cap at all — a material fallback failure.

Preferred is not complete. To reach it the drafter must add, in operative language: (i) a greater-of floor — "the greater of (a) fees paid or payable by Ono in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000"; (ii) carve-outs for breach of data protection and security obligations, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights; and (iii) an express statement that Ono's payment obligations under this Agreement are not "damages" subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: Section 16.5 and all surrounding text are untouched, nothing favourable is deleted, and the insertion is a single concise sentence for an otherwise missing clause. The parenthetical "(including under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2)" is not an extra — it tracks the indemnity sources 16.5 itself names, avoiding a mismatch between the two provisions.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is left undefined, no cross-reference dangles, and 16.7 does not contradict 16.5's proviso that the consequential-damages waiver does not apply to gross negligence or willful misconduct or limit third-party indemnity amounts.

Watch item (not a defect on these facts): Section 16.7 cites Article 10 both as an indemnification source and as the confidentiality article, mirroring the Agreement's own drafting in 16.5. If Array reads Article 10 as confidentiality only, tighten to "indemnification obligations under this Agreement (including Sections 16.1 and 16.2 and any indemnity in Article 10)" to avoid an argument about scope.

Basis note for negotiation: "fees and other amounts payable by Ono" is broader than the playbook's "fees paid or payable"; it is acceptable at the fallback (it raises the cap for both Parties) but should be aligned to "fees paid or payable" if the preferred greater-of formula is inserted.
